text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- An Airbus 320 aircraft of Bulgaria's national carrier Balkan Airlines aircraft has been grounded at the Erfurt airport in Germany on Thursday morning due to unpaid debts to the airport worth 183,000 German marks, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
Another Balkan Airlines aircraft, Boeing 737, was delayed in Athens due to a bomb threat received 15 minutes before takeoff.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided on Thursday to postpone the introduction of maximum price limits on basic foods due to the new record-high main interest rate of 300 percent annual.
-- Eight out of the nine banks put under special supervision on Monday by the central bank (BNB) suspended payments until further notice, BNB officials said.
The ninth, the Yambol commercial bank however pays out firms' and citizens' deposits because the BNB has not banned it from servicing clients, the bank's sequestrator Radan Kanchev said.
-- Bulgarian banks' internal credit rose to 1,139.2 billion levs on August 30 from 1,125.6 billion levs a week earlier, preliminary central bank figures showed.
Citizens' and firms' deposits in foreign currency amounted to 311 billion levs at the end of August.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided on Thursday to raise petrol prices by 13-17 levs (0.42-0.56 cents) a litre and diesel fuel price by 22 levs (0.10 cents) to 90 levs (0.39 cents) per litre, effective on Friday.

-- Some $300 million from embargo-busting exports to rump Yugoslavia, drug trafficking and prostitution entered Bulgaria through its western and northeastern border two years ago, the Bulgarian National Bank's former governor Todor Valchev said.
-- Bulgaria's central bank raised the allowed limit for cash payments between traders in the country to 500,000 levs from 100,000 levs.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to raise the salaries of some 550,000 state employees by 30 percent from October 1.

-- Germany's press giant Westdeutsche Algemeine Zeitung Group will be the new owner of Bulgaria's newspapers Standart and 7 Dni Sport and of their new printing house, Bulgaria's state news agency BTA said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
